description: Mishipeshu, the 'Great Lynx' of the Ojibwe and other Great Lakes Anishinaabe peoples, is the foremost underwater being: a horned, scaled panther with palmed paws and a copper tail dwelling in the depths of big lakes. It stirs waves and whirlpools, breaks winter ice and drowns the careless, yet guards the copper of Lake Superior and can grant healing to those who approach respectfully.

research_notes: Attested and well documented, but the tribe attribution in the record is wrong: Mishipeshu (Mishibizhiw) belongs to the Ojibwe/Anishinaabe and other Great Lakes Algonquian peoples (Odawa, Potawatomi, Cree, Innu), NOT Iroquois as the fun_fact claims. Confirmed details: horned feline with scales and copper tail, lives in deep lakes (Michipicoten Island, Lake Superior), causes storms/whirlpools/drowning, guards copper, opposes Thunderbirds, can grant medicine power. Input's 'forest spirit/helpful' framing is off; it is a dangerous yet necessary water manitou.

description: Monster Slayer (Naayéé' Neizghání) is the elder of the Navajo Hero Twins, sons of Changing Woman and the Sun. Armed by his father with flint armor and lightning arrows, he and his brother Born-for-Water slew the Anayé, the unnatural monsters that were killing the Diné, among them the giant Yé'iitsoh, making the world safe for the People. He remains a model of courage for young Navajo today.

research_notes: Fully attested and correctly attributed to Navajo (Diné). Some accounts say Monster Slayer was fathered by the Sun and his brother by the Moon. The generic 'forest spirit' archetype is wrong for this culture hero.

description: Mothman is a modern American cryptid of Point Pleasant, West Virginia: a gray, man-sized winged being with glowing red eyes, first reported in Nov 1966 near the abandoned TNT munitions site. Skeptical explanations: sandhill crane (Smith), barred owl (Nickell). Correctly attributed.
